whatItClaims: Risk settings adjustable before the first live trade.
A partner broker holding funds and executing orders.
Withdrawals processed in under a day, per the page.
No prior trading experience required.
AI and algorithmic market analysis producing signals and suggested entries.
whatWeChecked: The security claims: encryption and account protection statements.
The withdrawal path: steps and any fees the page omits.
The ownership trail: who operates the platform and where.
The support channels: live chat, email or phone availability.
The fine print: clauses that qualify the headline promises.
The fee framing: no platform fees, but spreads embedded in every trade.

steps.text: Fund US$300 via card or transfer to activate the trading balance.

pros: Risk settings before the first trade.
A browser dashboard - nothing to install.
redFlags: No regulator, licence or audit named anywhere.
Marketing numbers the fine print quietly qualifies.
A support bullet that garbles two claims at once.

faqs.q: Does it offer a demo account?
faqs.a: Yes - a practice account is part of the package and runs alongside the live balance, which is the sensible first step before risking the US$300 minimum.

faqs.q: How fast are withdrawals?
faqs.a: The page promises payouts within a day, but the processing detail is thin. Confirm the exact timeline and any fees with support before funding anything.

faqs.q: How much support does it offer?
faqs.a: Unclear - around-the-clock coverage is claimed, while other sections quote different figures. Ask support to reconcile them before you fund anything.

faqs.q: What happens after I sign up?
faqs.a: You confirm the account by email, fund US$300, set your risk preferences and choose automatic or manual mode. The demo account runs alongside while you learn.

faqs.q: Where is Hodgman Energy restricted?
faqs.a: The lists conflict - different sections of the site name different countries. Confirm your eligibility with support before depositing.

bottomLine: What we found is a real service wrapped in marketing that outruns its own fine print. Trade the service, not the marketing.
The verdict holds at 4.2: research it, demo it, and if you fund it, fund the minimum. The platform earns a careful start, not blind trust.
